title: Validation and Security Testing of AI Tools in GxP Settings
summary: Risk-based testing of LLM and ML tools used in quality, manufacturing or pharmacovigilance: accuracy, prompt injection, data leakage and audit-trail checks, packaged as validation evidence.

seo.title: GxP AI Validation and Security Testing | VipraTech
seo.description: Risk-based validation and adversarial testing for AI tools used in GxP work: accuracy, consistency, prompt injection, data leakage and audit trails.

problem.intro: Quality, manufacturing and safety teams are adopting AI tools: SOP assistants, deviation drafting, adverse event screening, vision inspection and AI features inside QMS or LIMS products. Traditional CSV scripts were written for deterministic software, and most teams have no method yet for testing an LLM's outputs or its exposure to prompt injection and data leakage.

pain_points.title: Non-deterministic outputs
pain_points.detail: The same question can produce different answers, so a single passed test script does not show the tool is fit for its intended use.

pain_points.title: A new attack surface
pain_points.detail: Documents, emails and user prompts can carry instructions that steer an LLM to leak data or ignore rules, and classic validation does not test for this.

pain_points.title: Vendor AI features arrive by update
pain_points.detail: QMS, LIMS and document platforms add AI features through releases, and QA must assess them without access to the vendor's model.

pain_points.title: Audit questions without evidence
pain_points.detail: Inspectors and customer auditors ask how an AI tool was validated and is controlled, and teams lack a structured evidence pack.

solution.overview: We run a risk-based assessment of an AI tool against its intended use. First we agree the use, risk level and acceptance criteria with QA and CSV. Then we build a test set from your own de-identified records and run it repeatedly to measure accuracy, consistency and refusal behaviour. In parallel we attack the tool: prompt injection through documents and inputs, attempts to retrieve other users' or sites' data, bypass of business rules, and checks that audit trails, access controls and electronic signatures behave as required. Findings come with reproducible evidence and fix guidance, assembled into a pack your validation team can reference.
capabilities: Intended-use and risk assessment aligned with your CSV or CSA procedure
Task-specific test sets from your de-identified records, run repeatedly to measure consistency
Prompt injection, jailbreak and data-leakage testing across documents, chat and API inputs
Access-control and site-segregation tests for retrieval-based assistants
Audit trail, electronic signature and change-control checks for the AI workflow
Re-runnable regression suite for model, prompt or vendor version changes

workflow.title: Define intended use and risk
workflow.detail: With QA and CSV we document what the tool is for, who relies on it and the GxP impact of a wrong output.

workflow.title: Build test sets
workflow.detail: We create functional cases from your records and adversarial cases from known LLM attack patterns.

workflow.title: Run functional tests
workflow.detail: Each case runs several times and is scored against the acceptance criteria agreed in step one.

workflow.title: Run security tests
workflow.detail: We attempt prompt injection, data leakage, privilege escalation and rule bypass, recording every attempt.

workflow.title: Review findings
workflow.detail: Results are reviewed with QA, CSV and IT, and each failure is classed as acceptable, mitigated or blocking.

workflow.title: Deliver the evidence pack
workflow.detail: A report, test logs and a regression suite are handed over for your validation file.

inputs: Description of the AI tool, its users and intended use
Your CSV or CSA procedure and templates
De-identified sample records relevant to the use
Test environment access with role-based accounts
Vendor documentation for third-party AI features
outputs: Functional test results with repeat-run consistency
Security findings with severity, evidence and fix guidance
human_in_the_loop: QA and CSV approve the intended use, risk level and acceptance criteria before testing starts, and decide how each finding is dispositioned. We provide evidence and recommendations; the validation decision stays with your quality unit.
integrations: The AI tool under test (web interface, API or vendor platform)
QMS for change control and CAPA records
Identity provider for role-based test accounts
CI pipeline for regression runs, where available
guardrails: Testing only in agreed environments under written authorisation
De-identified or synthetic data in all test sets
No testing against production patient or batch data
Findings shared only with named stakeholders
Regression suite re-run after any model, prompt or version change
compliance_notes: Evidence is structured to support validation under 21 CFR Part 11 and EU GMP Annex 11, using risk-based approaches such as ISPE GAMP 5 and FDA's Computer Software Assurance guidance.
EU regulators consulted in 2025 on a draft GMP Annex 22 on artificial intelligence; the pack is organised so it can be mapped to the final text.
Security testing references the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications and the NIST AI RMF.

pilot.scope: One AI tool with a defined GxP use, such as an SOP assistant or an adverse event screening model, tested in a non-production environment.
deliverables: Test execution logs and findings report

what_we_measure.how: Functional test cases scored by your subject matter experts or against reference answers.
Agreement of answers across repeated runs of the same test case.
Successful attack attempts classed on an agreed severity scale.
Sampled user and system actions checked for a complete, attributable audit record.

faqs.q: Does this replace our CSV team?
faqs.a: No. We bring AI-specific test methods and attack techniques, and your CSV team owns the validation approach and approvals. Deliverables are written to fit your existing templates.

faqs.q: Can you test a vendor's AI feature we cannot see inside?
faqs.a: Yes, as a black-box test through the interface your users have. We test behaviour against your intended use and data, which is what your risk assessment needs.

faqs.q: How often should testing be repeated?
faqs.a: After any change to the model, prompts, retrieval data or vendor version, and as part of periodic review. The regression suite makes repeat runs quick.
No. We test in a non-production environment with de-identified or synthetic data, under written authorisation from your IT and QA teams.
